newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa suspends Rwandan weapons deal.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa suspends Rwandan weapons deal.

text.p: South Africa announced on Wednesday it had suspended a deal to supply arms worth around 86.8 million rand ($18.5 million) to the Rwandan government.

"After high-level consultation with leaders in the Great Lakes region and reports of cross-border incursions by Rwandan armed forces (into Zaire), the supply of arms to the government of Rwanda has temporarily been suspended," the foreign affairs department said in a statement.
The statement said a committee which oversees South Africa's weapons sales would review the Rwanda decision "when the situation in the Great Lakes region is normalised".

Committee chairman Kader Asmal said earlier this week that South Africa had so far delivered only armoured personnel carriers to Rwanda, but the government declined to give details of the contract which is also believed to include small arms.
Human rights observers say the Great Lakes region is awash with weapons from various countries, including South Africa.

In the past few weeks in eastern Zaire ethnic Tutsi rebels, with the support of the Rwandan army, have been battling Zairean government troops and South Africa came in for criticism for a decision two months ago to lift a ban on arms sales to Rwanda.
Human rights groups have appealed to the international community to stop weapons from reaching troubled Central Africa.
Rivalry between majority Hutus and minority Tutsis has troubled Rwanda and Burundi for generations, sparking genocidal massacres in 1994.

A U.N. report earlier said that Hutu rebels in eastern Zaire had been supplied with arms from Europe and South Africa, which sold weapons to Rwanda's Hutu dominated government before it was overthrown bu ethnic Tutsis in 1994.
